title: Decision-Making Behavior Evaluation Framework for LLMs under Uncertain Context

bias_targets.methodology: Assigning male or female identities to LLM personas and evaluating variations in decision-making parameters (risk preference, probability weighting, and loss aversion) through multiple-choice lottery games.
Embedding different age groups into LLM personas and measuring shifts in behavioral economics parameters using probabilistic multiple-choice lists.
Assigning varying education levels (e.g., below lower secondary to graduate degrees) to personas and estimating the impact on LLM risk and loss aversion tendencies.
Evaluating decision-making behavior changes when LLMs are prompted with personas of different marital statuses (never married, married, widowed, divorced).
Comparing the decision-making parameters of LLMs when their prompted personas are assigned rural versus urban living areas.
Injecting different sexual orientations (heterosexual, homosexual, bisexual, asexual) into personas to observe differences in the models' risk-taking and loss aversion.
Comparing the decision-making behaviors and probability weighting tendencies of LLMs when prompted with physically-disabled versus able-bodied personas.
Assigning distinct racial backgrounds (African, Hispanic, Asian, Caucasian) to personas and measuring discrepancies in financial decision-making parameters.
Embedding religious affiliations (Jewish, Christian, Atheist, Religious) in prompts and evaluating the effects on LLM risk preferences and loss aversion.
Assigning specific political beliefs and affiliations to personas to analyze how political context shifts the models' decision-making under uncertainty.
